questions.problem: Let $a=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}]$ and $b=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 14 \\ -1\end{aligned}].$ Find the vector projection of $b$ onto $a.$
questions.worked_solution:
Using the formula for the vector projection, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{a}\,b & =\frac{a\cdot b}{a\cdot a}a \\  & =\frac{{a}_{x}{b}_{x}+{a}_{y}{b}_{y}+{a}_{z}{b}_{z}}{{a}_{x}^{2}+{a}_{y}^{2}+{a}_{z}^{2}}a \\  & =\frac{3\cdot 1+0\cdot 14+2\cdot (-1)}{{3}^{2}+{0}^{2}+{2}^{2}}a \\  & =\frac{1}{13}⟨3,0,2⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{3}{13},0,\frac{2}{13}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Let $c=[\begin{aligned}8 \\ -2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]$ and $d=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1 \\ -2\end{aligned}].$ Find the vector projection of $c$ onto $d.$
questions.worked_solution:
Using the formula for the vector projection, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{d}\,c & =\frac{c\cdot d}{d\cdot d}d \\  & =\frac{{c}_{x}{d}_{x}+{c}_{y}{d}_{y}+{c}_{z}{d}_{z}}{{d}_{x}^{2}+{d}_{y}^{2}+{d}_{z}^{2}}d \\  & =\frac{8\cdot 3+(-2)\cdot (-1)+(-1)\cdot (-2)}{{3}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+(-2)^{2}}d \\  & =\frac{28}{14}⟨3,-1,-2⟩ \\  & =2⟨3,-1,-2⟩ \\  & =⟨6,-2,-4⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Let $a=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ -2\end{aligned}]$ and $b=[\begin{aligned}x \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}].$ Given that the projection of $a$ onto $b$ is the zero vector, find the value of $x.$
questions.worked_solution:
Since $a$ is a nonzero vector, its projection onto another nonzero vector $b$ equals the zero vector only when the vectors are perpendicular. 

So, we must have

$$
a⊥b\,⟹\,a\cdot b=0.
$$

Computing the dot product, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot b & ={a}_{x}\cdot {b}_{x}+{a}_{y}\cdot {b}_{y}+{a}_{z}\cdot {b}_{z} \\  & =2\cdot x+1\cdot 2+(-2)\cdot (-1) \\  & =2x+4.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting the dot product equal to $0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot b & =0 \\ 2x+4 & =0 \\ 2x & =-4 \\ x & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $r$ is a nonzero vector, its projection onto another nonzero vector $s$ equals the zero vector only when the vectors are perpendicular. 

So, we must have

$$
r⊥s\,⟹\,r\cdot s=0.
$$

Computing the dot product, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}r\cdot s & ={r}_{x}\cdot {s}_{x}+{r}_{y}\cdot {s}_{y}+{r}_{z}\cdot {s}_{z} \\  & =(-5)\cdot n+1\cdot (-2)+3\cdot 4 \\  & =-5n-2+12 \\  & =10-5n.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting the dot product equal to $0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r\cdot s & =0 \\ 10-5n & =0 \\ n & =2.\end{aligned}
$$
